blocks.text: I can use correct word order when two objects are in a sentence, and can use plural indirect and direct object pronouns.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: A word that takes the place of a noun, like ‘it’, ‘you’, ‘she’.
A noun in the accusative case, directly affected by the action of the verb.
A noun in the dative case, indirectly affected by the action of the verb.

blocks.text: Testing yourself on vocabulary is like playing a game to train your brain.

items: By making your brain find the answers, the words stick in your memory for longer.
Testing yourself gives your memory little boosts to keep it strong.
It shows you which words you know well and which ones you need to practise more.

blocks.q: Match the German to the English.

blocks.text: Use pronouns in place of a noun.

items: Direct object pronouns replace the direct object and are in the accusative case.
Indirect object pronouns replace the indirect object and are in the dative case.

blocks.text: Singular examples: direct mich = me, ihn = him / it; indirect mir = to me, ihm = to him / it.

slides.title: Uns and euch do both jobs

blocks.text: Euch and uns are used as both direct and indirect object pronouns.

items: Mutti sieht {euch}. (direct object: Mum sees you)
Opa gibt {euch} Kuchen. (indirect object: Grandpa gives cake to you)

blocks.text: ‘Uns’ (‘us’, ‘to us’) and ‘euch’ (‘you’, ‘to you’, plural) look the same in the accusative and the dative.

items.q: Opa gibt ___ Kuchen. (Grandpa gives them cake.)
Wir wollen ___ sehen. (We want to see them.)
Wir wünschen ___ eine gute Reise. (We wish you (plural) a good journey.)

blocks.text: When a sentence has both a direct object noun and an indirect object noun, the indirect object noun always comes first.
Another example: Ich kaufe dem Lehrer die Blumen. (I am buying the teacher the flowers.)
When one of the objects is a pronoun, the pronoun is always the first object in the sentence. It does not matter what case the pronoun is in.

items: Ich bringe {es} dem Lehrer. (direct object pronoun first)
Ich bringe {ihm} das Buch. (indirect object pronoun first)

blocks.label: Watch out!
blocks.text: The direct object does not always come before the indirect object. If one object is a pronoun, the pronoun comes first, whether it is direct or indirect. Only when both objects are nouns does the indirect object come first.

blocks.q: Sort the sentences by their objects.
columns: A pronoun is the first object

items.text: Ich zeige ihr mein neues Kleid.
Alastair gibt seinem Freund das Handy.
Mia schenkt ihrer Mutter einen Kuchen.

blocks.q: Which kind of pronoun is the pronoun object in each sentence?

items.text: Ich zeige ihr mein neues Kleid.

blocks.q: Which sentence uses the correct word order?

options: Ich kaufe meinem Vater das Heft.
Ich kaufe das Heft meinem Vater.

blocks.text: The head teacher writes an email to the students. Look at the word order.

items: Nächste Woche erzählt ihr {uns} die ganzen Details.

blocks.q: What do these sentences have in common?
options: A pronoun (euch or uns) comes first, then the noun object
The noun object comes first, then the pronoun
blocks.why: Euch and uns are pronouns, so they come before the noun objects (die Wahrheit, ein Beispiel, die ganzen Details).

items: In sentences with two objects, if one is a pronoun, the pronoun is first, whether it is a direct or indirect pronoun.
If both objects are nouns, the indirect object comes before the direct object: Ich kaufe dem Lehrer die Blumen.
Use ‘uns’ (‘to us’, ‘us’) as both an indirect and a direct object pronoun.
Use ‘euch’ (‘to you’, ‘you’ - plural) as both an indirect and a direct object pronoun.

flashcards.front: In a sentence with two objects, where does a pronoun object go?
flashcards.back:
First, whether it is a direct or an indirect object pronoun.

Ich bringe es dem Lehrer.

flashcards.front: In a sentence with two object nouns, which object comes first?
flashcards.back:
The indirect object.

Ich kaufe dem Lehrer die Blumen.
us / to us. It is used as both a direct and an indirect object pronoun.
you / to you (plural). It is used as both a direct and an indirect object pronoun.

flashcards.front: Which plural pronoun means ‘them’ as a direct object?
Say in German: ‘We wish you (plural) a good journey.’
flashcards.back: Wir wünschen euch eine gute Reise.

flashcards.front: Say in German: ‘I’m buying you (plural) the exercise books.’
Does the case of a pronoun change which object comes first?
flashcards.back: No. It doesn’t matter what case the pronoun is in: the pronoun is always the first object.
A noun in the dative case, indirectly affected by the action of the verb.
A noun in the accusative case, directly affected by the action of the verb.

flashcards.back: Making your brain find the answers helps the words stick in your memory for longer, and it shows you which words to practise more.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: A school exchange: plural direct and indirect object pronouns
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question in German unless it asks for English. Write the whole sentence where asked.

questions.prompt: Task A: Write in German: The teacher is strict.
questions.explanation: Der Lehrer = the teacher, streng = strict.

questions.prompt: Task A: Write in German: She likes his art.
questions.explanation: Sie mag = she likes, seine Kunst = his art.

questions.prompt: Task A: Write in German: I win your game.
questions.explanation: gewinnen = to win, das Spiel = game.

questions.prompt: Task A: Write in German: at 12 o’clock
Task A: Write in German: for example
Task B: Ich habe einen Kilt. Ich zeige ___ Wolfgang. (I show it to Wolfgang.) Which pronoun fills the gap: ihn or es?
questions.explanation: ‘Kilt’ is masculine (einen Kilt), so the direct object pronoun is ‘ihn’. A pronoun comes before the noun ‘Wolfgang’.

questions.prompt: Task B: Wir wünschen ___ eine gute Reise. (We wish you (plural) a good journey.) Which pronoun fills the gap?
Task B: Ihr schreibt ___ viele E-Mails. (You write us lots of emails.) Which pronoun fills the gap?
questions.explanation: ‘Uns’ means ‘(to) us’; it is the same whether it is a direct or an indirect object pronoun.

questions.prompt: Task B: Write in German: I’m buying you (plural) the exercise books.
questions.explanation: The pronoun ‘euch’ comes first, then the noun ‘die Hefte’.
